answer: Charity-receipt identity: an identity is granted only when a charity confirms a donation tied to one key. The applicant gives $75 to an approved charity; the rail signs a receipt on payment binding it to one key, and the charity posts each receipt hash to the river, its public stream of gifts. The registry admits it only if its hash appears in the river before a 30-day horizon expires, rejects reused hashes, and issues one non-transferable onyx credential. Forging 1,000 puppets costs $75,000 with no bulk discount, since each credential needs its own receipt; an honest user pays once.
